scope.reviewed: 148-byte dispatcher logic, fresh history descriptor/count accesses, stride calculation, child call arguments, copy gate, registers and replay

findings.result: The complete independently decoded 148-byte body agrees with the pseudocode: saves R4-R11, captures current count before guards, skips buffers for count 0/255 but still writes the saved count through freshly loaded row+60/history pointer, handles prior count 255 as zero reuse, otherwise uses min counts, calls 49E6 with (row,current,history), and calls 49D4(config,current,history) for remaining entries. Current advances by 8; history advances by 8*((row word112 >> 8)&255). The saved count is written to history+4 at the shared epilogue; R0 is incidental.

All candidate pins match; the isolated 120-case replay is byte-identical. It asserts 49E6 argument order, original 49D4 copy behavior for gated cases, count updates, full history buffer contents and preserved high registers/SP. The 49E6 no-op is controlled, so no stronger child semantics follow.

limitations: Only counts {0,1,2,3,255}, prior counts {0,1,3,255}, configured strides {0,1,2}, and copy mode {0,2} are exercised.
Aliasing, concurrent mutation, caller closure, and general 49E6 semantics remain unresolved.
No canonical admission or C implementation.

checks.command: isolated replay and full-body independent Thumb decode
